answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a costly, verifiable stake: every agent posts a bond that is locked until its work is validated, so creating thousands of fake agents costs thousands of bonds. Like a mesa that stands because its rock is solid, reputation builds only on settled, paid-for work, and like a jetty that guides ships in one at a time, admissions are throttled so no single actor floods the queue. Verification data is kept crystal clear in a public ledger, so peers can audit each identity's history and slash any agent caught duplicating work.
